correctness.rationale: For target (s,p), predecessor solutions are the affine fibers of additive \(L_s(x)=x^2+sx\). Chain valuation gives exactly two disjoint cosets of J^(k-v) of size q^v when \(2v<k\), and exactly J^ceil(k/2) when \(2v\ge k\); multiplying |s|-strata by |Im L_s| gives all counts. Sharp maximum compares two attained root sizes; all boundary cases \(k=1\), zero s and collisions \(q=2\) are included. Direct forward enumeration across 16 tested \((q,k)\) cases reproduced all multiplicities; tests are finite support, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2012 Vieta quadratic-root reduction is known; 2017 covers only a squarefree-ring upper bound. Primary 2026 work on components and cycles does not give the all-characteristic-two chain-ring indegree spectrum. Seven targeted mathematical-registry searches returned no equivalent; material full-text comparisons and accessible ledger comparisons found none. The detailed closest implication distinctions and residual risks are recorded; search absence alone is not treated as proof of priority.
residual_risks: The full 2013 Ang–Shulte article and 2022 Daoub–Shafah–Lipkovski paper were not inspected; their abstracts target sources and cycles. An equivalent in-degree census under another notation remains a historical-priority risk.

Some September/October historical ledgers were inaccessible; accessible current and preceding week were searched for overlapping claims. Database retrieval and topic partition are not uniqueness proofs.

value.rationale: The exact histogram addresses the previously noted possibility of indegree greater than two in nonreduced finite-ring structure graphs. It gives a natural uniform invariant of all characteristic-two chain rings (not isolated small cases), pinpoints a sharp nilpotent-depth parity transition, and quantifies how many vertices have no predecessors and every possible branching degree. These data are not determined by connected-component or cycle counts and inform inverse-tree branching. No paper-sized downstream theorem is asserted.
